standing_summary: Tokenisation of securities is the one area of UK digital-asset regulation that is genuinely in force today, running on statutory powers wholly separate from the not-yet-effective FSMA 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026. The Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS) was created by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (Digital Securities Sandbox) Regulations 2023 (SI 2023/1398), made under HM Treasury's FMI-sandbox powers in FSMA 2023, in force since 8 January 2024 and amended by SI 2025/93 (laid 30 January 2025, covering money-laundering-regulation interaction and other technical points); per the instrument's own regulation 13, the sandbox regulations cease to have effect on 8 January 2029, and the Bank and FCA must report on its operation by 10 January 2028. The DSS lets firms test operating a trading venue or performing central-securities-depository functions (notary, settlement, maintenance) for digital securities on distributed, programmable ledgers, progressing through four gates from initial testing (Gate 1) to live business under limits (Gate 2), scaling (Gate 3), and a possible permanent regime (Gate 4). In a joint statement on 18 May 2026, the Bank and the FCA said they continue to work with '16 firms on the live issuance and settlement of tokenised assets' through the DSS -- language repeated verbatim in both regulators' own press releases that day. The Bank's own public DSS Dashboard, however, lists 15 named sandbox entrants (approved between 12 December 2024 and 4 December 2025), all shown as having passed only Gate 1, with the dashboard's own explanatory text stating that a Gate 1 entrant 'does not have permission to undertake any live activity' until approved at Gate 2 -- an apparent tension between the regulators' narrative description and their own published entrant data that this pillar state flags rather than resolves (see open items). The same 18 May 2026 joint statement published a Call for Input, 'The future of tokenisation -- a joint vision from the authorities for UK wholesale markets,' seeking industry views (deadline 3 July 2026) on scaling tokenisation of bonds, equities and fund units, alongside a Bank commitment to launch a live synchronisation service targeted for 2028, work on enabling tokenised assets as collateral, and consultation on extending RTGS/CHAPS settlement hours toward near-24/7 operation; the authorities said the responses would inform a joint FCA/Bank roadmap, with a feedback statement targeted for summer 2026 -- not yet published as of this pillar state's generation date. Separately, HM Treasury is running its own tokenisation pilot: on 12 February 2026 HM Treasury announced that HSBC, using its Orion digital-assets platform, had been selected -- following an Invitation to Tender published in October 2025 -- as platform provider for the pilot issuance of a Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT), a short-dated, digitally native gilt to be issued on a platform operating within the DSS and kept independent of the government's main debt-management programme; Ashurst LLP was named as legal adviser. No issuance date for DIGIT had been announced in the source fetched. On 13 July 2026, HM Treasury published the first of two reports from Christopher Woolard CBE -- appointed under the July 2025 Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy (WFMDS) as the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion -- setting out a framework and delivery roadmap for tokenising UK wholesale markets, developed with an industry Taskforce of more than fifty firms and two full Taskforce meetings of over eighty members and observers. The report sets ten priorities (Table 1) mapped to nine industry Action Groups (AG1-AG9, covering primary issuance and funds, secondary markets, collateral and prudential standards, FMI and cash leg, tax, legal, financial crime compliance and identity, resilience, and communications) plus a Champion-led Orchestration Group tasked with delivering a live, cross-border end-to-end repurchase-agreement (repo) transaction on blockchain, with an aim -- not a firm commitment -- of a live trial by spring 2027. Recommended supporting actions for Government and the Authorities include prioritising an immediate DIGIT pilot issuance 'no later than Q1 2027,' the Bank of England accepting DIGIT as Sterling Monetary Framework collateral, and review of CSD regulation, settlement finality rules, and the stablecoin regime's remaining elements (Table 2). The report itself corroborates this pillar state's earlier-flagged tension over DSS participation, stating that DSS participants 'have only entered the testing stage (Gate 1)' and must progress to Gate 2 before live business -- consistent with the Bank's DSS Dashboard data, not the more optimistic 'live issuance and settlement' framing in the regulators' 18 May 2026 joint statement. Action Group membership and precise tasks are due to be finalised in September 2026; the Champion's second report, on DLT adoption and interoperability, is due to the Chancellor by July 2027; industry feedback on this first report was invited by 4 September 2026. On 14 July 2026, HM Treasury published the recommendations of the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future (TTMF), a bilateral body HM Treasury and the US Treasury established following Chancellor Rachel Reeves' and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's September 2025 announcement; the Taskforce reported its recommendations to both finance ministries via the UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group (FRWG). Of its ten recommendations (five on digital assets, five on capital markets), two bear directly on this pillar: Recommendation 1 proposes a private-sector-led engagement group, established on a one-year basis, to test cross-border tokenised-asset use cases and share best practice; Recommendation 2 has the Bank of England, the FCA, the US CFTC and the US SEC seek common approaches to the regulatory treatment of tokenised assets, covering settlement finality of tokenised securities transactions and the potential eligibility of stablecoins and tokenised money market funds as margin collateral at central counterparties. Recommendation 5 separately records UK and US support for the Basel Committee's targeted review of cryptoasset prudential standards -- the same review already covered from the PRA's side in the Banking & Money pillar. None of the TTMF's recommendations creates a new UK legal obligation: they commit both governments to future engagement and joint regulatory work, not to specific rules.

open_items: There was an unresolved tension between the regulators' 18 May 2026 statement that 16 firms are engaged 'on the live issuance and settlement of tokenised assets' and the Bank of England's own DSS Dashboard, fetched during this research, which lists 15 named entrants all still at Gate 1 with no firm shown as approved for live activity at Gate 2 or beyond. The Wholesale Digital Markets Champion's first report (13 July 2026) corroborates the Dashboard's less advanced reading, stating that DSS participants 'have only entered the testing stage (Gate 1)' and must progress to Gate 2 before live business. Firm counts and 'live' characterisations should still be re-checked directly against the dashboard, which updates on a rolling basis, before being repeated as current fact.

The Call for Input's response deadline (3 July 2026) has passed as of this pillar state's generation date; the authorities targeted a feedback statement for 'summer 2026' with no fixed date, and none had been published in the sources fetched, including the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion's first report (13 July 2026), which welcomes the Call for Input but does not report a feedback statement having been published.

The FCA's own DSS overview page states the sandbox is operational 'until December 2028,' while the sandbox regulations themselves (SI 2023/1398, regulation 13) set cessation at 8 January 2029; this pillar state follows the statutory text as authoritative and flags the discrepancy rather than silently picking one.

The Call for Input also referenced PRA 'Dear CEO' letters on prudential treatment of tokenised assets and a fund-tokenisation policy statement; PRA prudential material belongs to the Banking & Money pillar and fund tokenisation may belong to Funds & ETFs -- neither is detailed here to avoid duplication, and should be independently sourced in those pillars.

No issuance date, size, or maturity had been announced for the DIGIT pilot in the primary source fetched (12 Feb 2026 gov.uk update). The Wholesale Digital Markets Champion's first report (13 July 2026) recommends that Government and the Authorities 'prioritise an immediate pilot issuance of DIGIT no later than Q1 2027' -- a recommendation to government, not a confirmed HM Treasury commitment as of this pillar state's generation date -- and should be re-checked against any subsequent HM Treasury DIGIT update.

The Digital Markets Champion Industry Taskforce's nine Action Groups (AG1-AG9) were newly proposed in the 13 July 2026 first report; their precise membership and tasks were due to be finalised in September 2026 and had not been finalised as of this pillar state's generation date.

The Champion's second report, covering DLT adoption and interoperability recommendations, is due to the Chancellor by July 2027 per the Champion's Terms of Reference; not yet published as of this pillar state's generation date.

Industry feedback on the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion's first report was invited by 4 September 2026; this pillar state does not reflect any resulting revisions, which would only appear in the Champion's second report or a later published update.

The Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future's recommendations (14 July 2026) are joint HM Treasury/US Treasury policy commitments to future engagement -- e.g. a one-year private-sector group and joint regulator work on tokenised-asset standards -- not new UK rules; Recommendation 1's one-year engagement period has no stated fixed end date.

The UK-US joint statement on stablecoins, published the same day as the TTMF recommendations, is covered primarily in the Stablecoins pillar; only the tokenised-asset and margin-collateral elements of the TTMF recommendations are reflected here to avoid duplicating that content.
